chain.label: Unpowered, aerodynamically-balanced ATR aileron design vulnerable to hinge-moment reversal
chain.trigger: unpowered aileron control systems can be susceptible to undesirable aileron hinge moment changes (including asymmetric hinge moment reversals) and subsequent uncommanded aileron deflections

chain.label: ATR failed to disclose known hinge-moment-reversal hazard after prior icing incidents
chain.trigger: ATR failed to disseminate adequate warnings and guidance to operators...and ATR failed to develop additional airplane modifications, which led directly to this accident

caused_by.evidence: ATR recognized the reason for the aileron behavior in the previous incidents and determined that ice accumulation behind the deice boots...would cause the ailerons to become unstable

chain.label: DGAC's inadequate continuing-airworthiness oversight of the ATR 42/72
chain.trigger: the DGAC's inadequate oversight of the ATR 42 and 72, and its failure to take the necessary corrective action to ensure continued airworthiness in icing conditions

chain.label: FAA icing certification requirements and oversight did not account for freezing rain/large-droplet icing
chain.trigger: the FAA's failure to ensure that aircraft icing certification requirements...adequately accounted for the hazards that can result from flight in freezing rain and other conditions not specified in 14 CFR Part 25, Appendix C

chain.label: No unusual-attitude/advanced-maneuvers or aileron-hinge-moment-reversal recovery training provided to crew
chain.trigger: there were no formal 'advanced maneuvers' or 'unusual attitude' training sessions being conducted

caused_by.evidence: ATR did not provide, nor did the regulatory authorities require, training or guidance to pilots about the roll axis 'anomalies' or the recovery techniques

chain.label: Flight 4184 intermittently encountered supercooled large-droplet icing beyond the certification envelope while holding, forming an ice ridge aft of the deice boots
chain.trigger: the airplane...intermittently encountered supercooled cloud and drizzle/rain drops, the size and water content of which exceeded those described in the icing certification envelope

caused_by.evidence: the current process by which aircraft are certified using the Appendix C icing envelope is inadequate and does not require manufacturers to sufficiently demonstrate the airplane's capabilities under a sufficiently realistic range of icing conditions

chain.label: Ice-induced airflow separation caused a sudden aileron hinge-moment reversal and uncommanded aileron deflection as flaps retracted and AOA rose
chain.trigger: the ailerons rapidly deflected to 13.43 degrees RWD, the autopilot disconnected

caused_by.evidence: a ridge of ice accreted beyond the deice boots
unpowered aileron control systems can be susceptible to undesirable aileron hinge moment changes

chain.label: Autopilot automatically disconnected as aileron deflection rate exceeded its monitoring threshold, removing automatic roll stabilization
chain.trigger: the autopilot could not control the aileron deflection rate, which exceeded that allowed by the autopilot so the autopilot disconnected

caused_by.evidence: the aileron deflection rate...exceeded the deflection rate capability of...the autopilot servo motor

chain.label: Airplane entered repeated, rapid roll excursions through inverted attitude that the crew could not arrest with available techniques
chain.trigger: The airplane rolled rapidly to the right...rolled again to the right for 9 seconds, rolling approximately 1 and 1/4 times

caused_by.evidence: the airplane rolled rapidly to the right until reaching 77 degrees RWD
power will be removed from the autopilot aileron servo motor and servo clutch
without the knowledge of the ice-induced aileron hinge moment reversal problem, the flightcrew's execution of conventional unusual attitude recovery techniques may have been ineffective

chain.label: Low-altitude high-speed pull-out from the near-inverted dive overloaded the wings and tail
chain.trigger: the elevator position and vertical acceleration began to increase rapidly...experiencing a vertical acceleration of 3.6 G

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was at an airspeed of 375 KIAS...with 5 degrees of nose-up elevator, and was experiencing a vertical acceleration of 3.6 G

chain.label: Airplane struck a soybean field partially inverted, nose down, after in-flight structural failure of the outboard wings and tail
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted a wet soybean field partially inverted, in a nose down, left-wing-low attitude

caused_by.evidence: the outboard 10 feet of the left and right wings, as well as the horizontal stabilizer, separated from the airframe at a very low altitude

chain.label: All 68 occupants killed; accident unsurvivable
chain.trigger: the captain, first officer, 2 flight attendants and 64 passengers received fatal injuries

caused_by.evidence: The accident was not survivable because the impact forces exceeded human tolerances
